ut_jungle_on_the_aquarius_plateau.blurb: The Jungle is a high, remote crag area on the Aquarius Plateau in south-central Utah, at roughly 10,400 feet among subalpine forest. The cliffs are volcanic tuff and lava that breaks into sharp edges; the rock runs from very good to loose, so rockfall deserves respect. Trad and sport are almost evenly split, mostly 5.9 to 5.11, with long cracks on offer and a small bouldering spot with softer rock. Lower Jungle is the busiest area, followed by Shangri La, Shattered Sea and the Air Strip. North-facing sections like the Lower Jungle stay the most sheltered from the sun, thunderstorms are common in late July and August, and fall is called the most pristine time.

ok_mount_scott.blurb: Mount Scott rises in the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge in southwest Oklahoma, and its climbing is on granite, in a wilderness setting. Walks in are the briefest anywhere in the refuge. Bouldering is the biggest share, particularly on the Talus Slope and several smaller boulder groups, while Upper and Lower Mount Scott hold most of the trad and sport lines, with a few top-ropes. Boulder problems cluster from V1 to V5, and roped climbs run mostly from 5.6 to 5.11. The Crucible and Glasgow are among the other larger sub-areas.

wv_bozoo.blurb: Bozoo is a short cliff band and boulder field above the New River near Bozoo, in southern West Virginia. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with a wide spread of problems, mostly V2 to V6 and a few much harder. The cliffs carry mainly trad routes, an occasional bolted line and easily rigged top-ropes, with grades from 5.6 to 5.12. The fine-grained sandstone is compact and hard, and most lines face south, so it dries quickly after cold or snowy weather, while summer foliage adds shade. Bozoo Bouldering is by far the largest sub-area, followed by the Iceberg, Savory and Rigor walls. Crowds are light.

mt_paradise_valley.blurb: Paradise Valley follows the Yellowstone River south of Livingston, Montana, between the Gallatin Range and the Absaroka and Beartooth mountains. The climbing is varied: bouldering and sport lead, with some trad, alpine routes and a little ice. Allenspur is the main sport crag, on limestone that faces southwest, which makes it a go-to on cold days and sometimes in winter; the rock is abrasive on skin. Yankee Jim and Pine Creek hold the boulders. Mill Creek offers shorter, tougher trad and sport lines in summer, and Mount Cowen has big alpine granite routes, best in July and August. Sport grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11.

nh_sundown_ledge.blurb: Sundown Ledge is the centerpiece of climbing along the eastern end of the Kancamagus Highway in New Hampshire's White Mountains. The largest share is bouldering in the separate Sundown Bouldering zone, spread over around ten sub-areas with problems from easy V0 to a handful at V9 and V10; some groups, such as the campground and first tier, suit beginners and families. The cliffs add trad and sport, with Main Cliff holding the most and Lost Horizon, Outback Cliff and the Far Cliff quieter. Roped climbs lean hard, mostly 5.10 to 5.13, with a few easier ones. Most visits focus on Main Cliff and Lost Horizon.
